paper.title: Efficient Online Lexicographic Generalized Low-Rank Matrix Bandits

settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards with lexicographic preference; ontology scope excludes multi-objective rewards.
unmapped: m objectives with vector-valued reward, each with its own GLM link and rank-<=r parameter matrix Theta_i in R^{d1 x d2}
lexicographic preference order; regret per objective w.r.t. lexicographically optimal arm
lexicographic trade-off assumption with parameter w (Assumption 5)
existence of exploration distribution with bounded score second moment M (Assumption 6)
bounded mean |mu_i| <= U and noise |eta| <= R
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t\in[T]$, the learner first observes the arm set $\SX\subseteq\R^{d_1\times d_2}$, selects an arm $\X_t\in\SX$, and then receives a stochastic reward vector $y_t=(y_{t,1},\ldots,y_{t,m})\in\R^m$... $\E[y_{t,i}\mid \X_t]=\mu_i(\langle \X_t,\Theta_i^*\rangle)$

symbols.W_sca: sum_{i=1}^{m} (1+w)^{i-1}, m = number of objectives, w = lexicographic trade-off parameter
symbols.M: bound on second moment of score function of exploration distribution
symbols.D_rr: minimum over objectives of r-th largest singular value of Theta_i

conditions: Assumptions 1-6 (rank <= r, ||Theta_i||_F <= S, ||X||_F <= 1, c_mu <= mu_i' <= L_mu, bounded rewards/noise, lexicographic trade-off w, exploration distribution with bounded score moment M)
U, R, L_mu, c_mu, S treated as constants
sqrt(M(d1+d2)r)/D_rr <= O((d1+d2)r) (scaling condition used in proof)
bound holds for every objective i in [m]
tuning: lambda_perp = c_mu T/(k log(1 + c_mu T/(k lambda_0))), k=(d1+d2)r-r^2

source.label: thm:scalar_lowglm
source.quote: Then, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, for every objective $i\in[m]$, the cumulative regret satisfies \[ R_i(T)= \widetilde O\!\left(W^{\rm sca}\cdot(d_1+d_2)r\sqrt{T}\right), \] where $W^{\rm sca}=\sum_{i=1}^m (1+w)^{i-1}$.

results.notes: Regret is per-objective pseudo-regret through means, holding w.p. 1-2delta. Multi-objective setting (out of scope). k_mu corresponds to the paper's L_mu.

symbols.M: bound on second moment of score function of exploration distribution
symbols.D_rr: minimum over objectives of r-th largest singular value of Theta_i

conditions: U, R, L_mu, c_mu, S treated as constants
sqrt(M(d1+d2)r)/D_rr <= O((d1+d2)r) (scaling condition used in proof)
bound holds for every objective i in [m]
tuning: same parameters as Theorem 1: T_1 ~ sqrt(M(d1+d2) r T log((d1+d2)m/delta))/D_rr, lambda_0 = max{1,c_mu/2}, lambda_perp = c_mu T/(k log(1+c_mu T/(k lambda_0))), S_perp as in Theorem 1

source.label: thm:lexi_lowglm_ucb
source.quote: Then, with probability at least $1-2\delta$, for every objective $i\in[m]$, the cumulative regret satisfies \begin{equation*} R_i(T)=\widetilde O\left(W_i^{\rm lex}\sqrt{m}\cdot(d_1+d_2)r\sqrt{T}\right), \end{equation*} where $W_i^{\rm lex} = 1+w+\cdots+w^{i-1}$.

results.notes: Per-objective regret through means w.p. 1-2delta; online Newton-step updates, O(T) total estimator-update cost. m here is the number of objectives (declared m_obj).
